speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you have knee pain after recent increased physical activity; please describe exactly where the pain is located, how it started, and if you heard a pop or felt instability at the time. To help narrow this down, how would you rate your pain on a scale of 0 to 10, and does it worsen with specific movements like squatting or twisting?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age, recent volleyball activity involving pivoting, and the worsening pain, did you experience a specific "pop" sound or sensation when the pain began yesterday? Also, does the knee currently feel unstable or give way, and is there significant swelling around the joint?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints). The location of pain over the medial tibia inferior to the patella, combined with recent increased activity and weight loss attempts, strongly suggests this diagnosis. I will now request imaging to confirm there is no associated stress fracture. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray_knee_anteroposterior.
